mitre.technique_name: Remote Services: Distributed Component Object Model

description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with remote machines by leveraging Distributed Component Object Model (DCOM). The adversary may then perform actions as the logged-on user. DCOM is transparent middleware that extends the functionality of Component Object Model (COM) beyond a local computer using remote procedure call (RPC) technology.
artifacts: RPC endpoint mapper connections (TCP/135) followed by DCOM activation traffic on dynamic high ports
DCERPC IRemoteSCMActivator RemoteCreateInstance requests targeting DCOM CLSIDs (e.g., MMC20.Application, ShellWindows, ShellBrowserWindow)
DCOM object activation referencing MMC20.Application (CLSID 49B2791A-B1AE-4C90-9B8E-E860BA07F889) for ExecuteShellCommand abuse
NTLMSSP NEGOTIATE/CHALLENGE/AUTH messages during DCOM bind using valid account credentials
SMB session setup (TCP/445) following DCOM activation for command output retrieval (dcomexec pattern)
DCERPC bind failures or ACCESS_DENIED responses when supplied credentials are invalid
NTLM authentication failures (STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE) during DCOM activation attempts
Remote WMI/DCOM-based process execution without prior interactive logon on the target

pcaps.name: Internal DCOM execution via MMC20 (impacket dcomexec)
pcaps.description: Internal authenticated DCOM lateral movement using impacket dcomexec.py with the MMC20.Application object, showing RPC endpoint mapper lookup, DCOM activation over dynamic high ports, and remote command execution on the target.

pcaps.name: Internal DCOM execution failed via MMC20 (impacket dcomexec)
pcaps.description: Internal DCOM lateral movement attempt using impacket dcomexec.py with the MMC20.Application object and an invalid password, showing RPC endpoint mapper lookup and NTLM authentication failure during DCOM activation.
